extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and practitioners filing or prosecuting Eurasian patent applications (EAPO) including via the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal requirements, timelines, fees, representation rules, and legal effects for obtaining and maintaining a Eurasian patent under the Eurasian Patent Convention (EAPC), including filing via the PCT regional phase. Useful for applicants and agents preparing or converting applications and for understanding post-grant consequences across Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting date of EAPC operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The starting date of operation under the Eurasian Patent Convention is January 1, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As from that date, the Eurasian Patent Office receives Eurasian patent applications and Eurasian patents can be sought in international applications under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting States (parties to the Convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: By December 31, 1995, nine States had deposited instruments of accession or ratification: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Republic of Moldova, Russian Federation, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are referred to as 'the Contracting States'; for each State's entry-into-force date see the corresponding EAPC Notification issued by WIPO. The granted Eurasian patent has effect in all Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to obtain a Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone—irrespective of nationality or domicile—may obtain a Eurasian patent for an invention by filing a single application with the Eurasian Patent Office in Moscow and making a single payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single application can produce patent effect across all Contracting States without regard to applicant nationality or residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for Eurasian applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The request part of an application for the grant of a Eurasian patent must be in Russian. Other parts of the Eurasian application may, at the moment of filing, be in Russian or in any other language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any parts not in Russian, a Russian translation must be furnished by the applicant within two months following the date of receipt by the Eurasian Patent Office of the Eurasian application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of facsimile filing and original-document requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Patent Office accepts the filing of applications by facsimile, but the signed original must reach the Office within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fax filing is permitted for speed/convenience but is conditional on timely submission of the signed original to validate the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic prosecution procedure and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure follows usual rules: examination as to form; search; publication after the expiry of 18 months from the priority date; substantive examination (done on request); and grant or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for substantive examination must be made before the expiry of six months from the date of publication of the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion into national applications after refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant of the Eurasian patent is refused, the applicant may transform his Eurasian application into national applications having the filing date and the priority date, if any, of the Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transformation may be made in those Contracting States in which the applicant wishes to obtain a national patent under the national procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary legal effect of a granted Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The granted Eurasian patent is not a bundle of national patents but has, in the Contracting States, a unitary legal effect governed by the Convention and the Patent Regulations adopted by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent's legal regime across Contracting States is governed centrally by the Convention/Regulations rather than by separate national patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: National jurisdiction for validity and infringement disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute concerning the validity in a given Contracting State, or an infringement in a given Contracting State, of a Eurasian patent will be decided by the national courts or other competent authorities of that State on the basis of the Convention and the Patent Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a decision has legal effect only in the territory of that Contracting State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court translation requirement in non-Russian States
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a dispute, any national court or other competent authority of a Contracting State in which Russian is not a State language may require that the plaintiff furnish to it a translation of the Eurasian patent in the State language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be prepared to provide translations for enforcement proceedings where required by local authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No designation of Contracting States at filing; designation at maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement and no possibility to designate Contracting States in the Eurasian patent application. The Eurasian patent has effect on the territory of all Contracting States from the date of its publication by the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, when annual maintenance fees are due and are paid, the owner must designate by name those Contracting States in which he wishes the effect of the patent to continue; designations must be addressed to the Eurasian Patent Office and patent maintenance fees must be paid at the same time. A separate fee is payable in respect of each designated Contracting State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the Eurasian Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has the right to be a representative before the national Patent Office of a Contracting State and who is registered with the Eurasian Patent Office as a patent agent may act as representative before the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the applicant does not have his residence or principal place of business in the territory of a Contracting State, he is required to be represented by such a registered patent agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing, examination, and grant fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee to be paid at the filing of a Eurasian application (the 'unitary procedural fee') is US$800, plus US$50 for each claim in excess of ten. This fee covers search and publication. A further amount of US$800 is payable when examination is requested. Finally, US$500 are payable when the Eurasian patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unitary procedural fee is reduced by 25% when the application, filed via the PCT, enters the regional phase before the Eurasian Patent Office and is accompanied by an international (PCT) search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing via PCT (regional phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: As from the starting date, Eurasian patents can be sought in international applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing via PCT and entering the regional phase before the Eurasian Patent Office may entitle the applicant to a 25% reduction of the unitary procedural fee if accompanied by an international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of registered agents, fee schedules, and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of registered patent agents, the schedule of fees and printed application (and other) forms are available from the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and agents should obtain these materials from the EAPO to ensure correct forms, current fees, and authorized representatives are used.
